To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a new multi-class classification algorithm, which reduces the computational complexity of classification tasks, and which is based on a novel formulation of the multi-class classification problem, where labels appear in terms of the inner products between them, in the same fashion as input data appear in terms of kernel inner products in kernel methods.
we present a method for multiclass classification that reduces the computational time of classification without sacrificing its generalisation performance.
we propose a new method for multi-class least-squares classification, with a complexity that is essentially independent of the total number of available classes.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following question: can we build a multi-class classifier with the same computational complexity as a binary one?
Multi-class least squares regression.
the development of a multi-class classification algorithm, with a computational time complexity that depends essentially on the number of samples, rather than on the number of classes.
the development of a multi-class classification technique, which is computationally efficient and generalizable.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is a multi-class classification method that is based on the least squares criterion, which is a very efficient algorithm for binary classification problems.
the method presented in this paper can be seen as a generalization of the well known one-vs-all scheme, with the advantage of reducing the computational cost of the multi-class task.
our method is a good choice for classification tasks where the number of classes is high.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the computational cost of multi-class classification is not necessarily dependent on the number available classes.
we propose an algorithm for multi-class least-squares classification, which is computationally as efficient as the binary least-squares classification.
we present a method to solve the multi-class classification problem at a computational cost comparable to the binary classification case.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the computational time of a multi-class classification task is independent of the number and of the complexity of the classes.
the complexity of the multi-class classification problem can be reduced to that of the binary classification problem.
the number of classes in a classification problem does not have to be a bottleneck for classification methods.
